key_insight: The paper repurposes hyperfine intermediate states in a two-photon EIT adiabatic CNOT gate to both stabilize adiabatic evolution and speed up population transfer, enabling fast high-fidelity control.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical route to shorter, more robust quantum gate times in Rydberg-atom hardware, which directly addresses coherence-time constraints in quantum processors.
method: Use an EIT-based adiabatic CNOT protocol with hyperfine intermediate states.
Exploit HISs in both the STAY pathway for adiabaticity and the TRANSFER pathway for faster population transfer.
Optimize pulse shapes and model decay effects across multiple intermediate states for realistic Cs implementations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports adiabatic gate fidelities above 0.9991 achieved in 0.3903 μs in realistic cesium atomic setups.
watch_item: Performance may be sensitive to decay from intermediate hyperfine states and to control precision in real hardware implementations.
paper_title: Fast Adiabatic Quantum Gates via Hyperfine Intermediate States
